bottleneck: Closed-loop neuromodulation — stimulating only when biomarkers indicate need — requires real-time detection of pathological brain states from noisy recordings, plus control algorithms that adapt without destabilizing the circuit. Biomarkers for most disorders are unreliable, latencies of 100-500 ms degrade control quality, and the long-term effects of adaptive stimulation on brain plasticity are unknown. Open-loop DBS persists because closing the loop is genuinely hard, and a miscalibrated closed loop could reinforce the pathology it aims to treat.
current_state: Responsive neurostimulation exists for epilepsy using simple detection; adaptive DBS for Parkinson's is in early trials. General closed-loop control across disorders is unsolved.

title: Closed-loop neuromodulation lacks reliable biomarkers
why_it_blocks: Continuous stimulation wastes battery, causes side effects, and habituates circuits. Without reliable state detection, neuromodulation cannot become the responsive, personalized therapy it promises to be.
